concept: exo DeepSeek V4 expert sharding (ShardedMoEV4) as EP substitute
summary: `ShardedMoEV4` is a wrapper class in exo's `auto_parallel.py` that does for `DeepseekV4MoE` what `ShardedMoE` does for other MoE layers, with one signature difference: the V4 MoE call takes `(x, input_ids)`, since the V4 MoE call also receives `input_ids`.

facts.text: `ShardedMoEV4` is a wrapper class in exo's `auto_parallel.py` that does for `DeepseekV4MoE` what `ShardedMoE` does for other MoE layers, with one signature difference: the V4 MoE call takes `(x, input_ids)`, since the V4 MoE call also receives `input_ids`.

The wrapper applies `sum_gradients(group)` to the input and `mx.distributed.all_sum(y, group)` to the output of the whole MoE block, then returns `y`. In inference `sum_gradients` is an identity in the forward pass (its all-sum is only in the backward rule), so each V4 MoE layer costs one all_sum.

`DeepseekV4ShardingStrategy` slices `ffn.switch_mlp.gate_proj` and `up_proj` all-to-sharded and `down_proj` sharded-to-all in place, and does the same for `shared_experts` when present. In place means each rank holds a slice of the intermediate dimension of every expert, not a subset of whole experts.
No `all_to_all` call and no expert-to-rank placement table exists in this file; its only gather calls are for pipeline output and the MiniMax q/k norm.

V4 attention is head-parallel with interleaved-per-group sharding: V4 reshapes the flat head dimension into `(o_groups, heads_per_group, head_dim)`, so each rank takes `heads_per_group / N` heads from every group, kept in group-major order. A contiguous block split would put heads in the wrong `wo_a` group.

The code asserts `n_heads % o_groups == 0` and `heads_per_group % world_size == 0`, then slices `wq_b` rows (stride `head_dim`) and `attn_sink`, and sets `attn.n_heads = o_groups * heads_per_group_per_rank`.

The attention output uses `wo_a` sharded-to-all in place (a block split on the input dimension) and `wo_b` wrapped in `_AllSumLinear`, which all-sums the partial `wo_a` output on every rank and then runs the unsharded `wo_b` replicated.

The `_AllSumLinear` docstring explains the choice: one collective per layer on the smaller of `n_groups * o_lora_rank` and hidden size; replicating `wo_b` costs about 30M FLOPs per layer at batch 1, less than "61 extra all_gathers/token".
So a V4 layer makes two all_sums (attention via `_AllSumLinear`, MoE via `ShardedMoEV4`), which is about 122 per token for 61 layers.

Loading is layer by layer with `mx.eval(layer)` and `mx.clear_cache()` after each, and `_slice_head_major_flat` makes a contiguous copy because a view would keep the full unsharded weight resident ("OOM on large V4").

exo depends on a fork for V4: `pyproject.toml` pins `mlx-lm` to `rltakashige/mlx-lm` branch `leo/deepseek-v4`, and pins `mlx` 0.32.0 on macOS to `rltakashige/mlx-jaccl-fix-small-recv` branch `address-rdma-gpu-locks`.
Upstream `ml-explore/mlx-lm` had no `mlx_lm/models/deepseek_v4.py` on main when fetched on 2026-10-04 (HTTP 404), so exo's V4 tensor parallelism depends on the fork.

Placement and load disagree: exo's placement test exempts V4 from the KV-head divisibility rule, but the V4 loader needs `heads_per_group % N == 0`, so a node count that passes placement can still fail at load with an assertion.
Rank-count limits follow `heads_per_group`, so the largest TP size is set by that number and not by hidden size or KV heads.
The replicated `wo_b` costs compute on every rank and grows with batch size, so the batch-1 saving may reverse for batched serving.

Because every rank reads a slice of every active expert, a V4 model that fits one Mac loses decode speed when sharded, as for other sliced-expert TP (see tensor-vs-pipeline-vs-expert-parallelism-for-moe.md).

Label versus mechanism. The concept's name treats the wrapper as expert sharding that stands in for expert parallelism. The code shows sliced-expert tensor parallelism. A source that says V4 "shards experts" (exo-cluster-software.md) means the slice, not whole-expert placement.

exo versus ds4 on the same model family. exo slices every expert on every rank and all-sums; ds4 gives each rank a contiguous half of the routed experts and exchanges partials. Neither source compares them on one machine pair.
Whether exo will add a true EP path for V4 now that the model has many small experts.
How large a share of V4 decode time the roughly 122 all_sums per token take under exo; no source read reports a V4 tensor-parallel benchmark through exo.
exo's `ShardedMoEV4` wraps `DeepseekV4MoE`, calls it with `(x, input_ids)`, applies `sum_gradients` before and `all_sum` after.
exo's `auto_parallel.py` has no `all_to_all` call.
In MLX's `sum_gradients` the forward pass is an identity and the all-sum is only in the vjp.
exo shards V4 attention heads interleaved per output group so that `wo_a`'s grouped weight mapping stays valid.
exo's V4 shard code asserts `heads_per_group % world_size == 0`.
exo's `_AllSumLinear` replicates `wo_b` on every rank to avoid 61 extra all_gathers per token.
exo shards V4 one layer at a time and copies sliced attention rows contiguously to free the full weight.
exo pins mlx-lm to the `leo/deepseek-v4` branch of `rltakashige/mlx-lm`.
Upstream mlx-lm main returned 404 for `deepseek_v4.py` on 2026-10-04.
A V4 layer in exo makes two all_sums, one after attention and one after the MoE block.
exo's V4 placement exemption and the loader's `heads_per_group` assertion can disagree.

CONTRADICTS: the concept label "as EP substitute" and the "shards experts" wording in exo-cluster-software.md: `ShardedMoEV4` slices the intermediate dimension of every expert on every rank in place; it places no whole experts on ranks.
